pr_title: Report event for the cases when probe returned Unknown result
pr_body:
This fix aims to expose in logs the cases when the Unknown result can be returned by the probe.

The attempt of this fix is to:

- Ensure that when a probe result is Unknown, a log entry is made;
- That an event is recorded and exposed when a probe result is Unknown.

issue_context.title: Report event for the cases when probe returned Unknown result
issue_context.body:
There are a few cases when the Unknown result can be returned by the probe. For example see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/106682.

It will be useful to expose those in logs and as an event similar to what we do for Warning: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/35f3fc59c1f29eebc8ff8705ecc3d4db7c4cbbc6/pkg/kubelet/prober/prober.go#L115

What needs to be done:

1. Implement logging and exposing event in case of `Unknown` probe result somewhere around https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/35f3fc59c1f29eebc8ff8705ecc3d4db7c4cbbc6/pkg/kubelet/prober/prober.go#L115
2. For each instance of probes potentially returning the `Unknown` result have a test that validates this test case. It may be either e2e test or unit test. You may find an example of e2e test that results in Unknown result from exec probe in one of the links from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/106682

I’m not sure if this fix is really necessary. 

Whenever `probe.Unknown` is returned, an error is also returned:
```
$ grep --exclude=*_test.go -R -n probe.Unknown pkg/kubelet pkg/probe
pkg/kubelet/prober/prober.go:147:			return probe.Unknown, "", err
pkg/kubelet/prober/prober.go:162:			return probe.Unknown, "", err
pkg/kubelet/prober/prober.go:182:		return probe.Unknown, "", fmt.Errorf("missing probe handler for %s:%s", format.Pod(pod), container.Name)
pkg/probe/exec/exec.go:82:		return probe.Unknown, "", err
```

So, if `Unknown` is returned, `probe errored` is emitted to logs and events:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/95d71c464a6a5f81ae36bddc86972b3b2a1c40a5/pkg/kubelet/prober/prober.go#L103-L105

Regarding `probe.Failure`, no error is returned except for one case:
```
$ grep --exclude=*_test.go -R -n probe.Failure pkg/kubelet pkg/probe
pkg/probe/http/http.go:99:		return probe.Failure, err.Error(), nil
pkg/probe/http/http.go:107:			return probe.Failure, "", err
pkg/probe/http/http.go:122:	return probe.Failure, failureMsg, nil
pkg/probe/tcp/tcp.go:56:		return probe.Failure, err.Error(), nil
pkg/probe/grpc/grpc.go:75:			return probe.Failure, fmt.Sprintf("timeout: failed to connect service %q within %v: %+v", addr, timeout, err), nil
pkg/probe/grpc/grpc.go:78:			return probe.Failure, fmt.Sprintf("error: failed to connect service at %q: %+v", addr, err), nil
pkg/probe/grpc/grpc.go:98:				return probe.Failure, fmt.Sprintf("error: this server does not implement the grpc health protocol (grpc.health.v1.Health): %s", stat.Message()), nil
pkg/probe/grpc/grpc.go:101:				return probe.Failure, fmt.Sprintf("timeout: health rpc did not complete within %v", timeout), nil
pkg/probe/grpc/grpc.go:109:		return probe.Failure, fmt.Sprintf("error: health rpc probe failed: %+v", err), nil
pkg/probe/grpc/grpc.go:113:		return probe.Failure, fmt.Sprintf("service unhealthy (responded with %q)", resp.GetStatus().String()), nil
pkg/probe/exec/exec.go:71:			return probe.Failure, string(data), nil
pkg/probe/exec/exec.go:76:				return probe.Failure, err.Error(), nil
```
The exception is here:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/95d71c464a6a5f81ae36bddc86972b3b2a1c40a5/pkg/probe/http/http.go#L107

Whether the result is `Unknown` or `Failure`, if the error is not `nil`, the result is ignored like #106682:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/95d71c464a6a5f81ae36bddc86972b3b2a1c40a5/pkg/kubelet/prober/worker.go#L294-L295

I think we can already distinguish whether a probe error is ignored or not by seeing whether the message is `probe errored` or `probe failed` though they sound a little confusing.

This complicates the code and makes an assumption that `probe.Unknown` will always come with non-nil error. We shouldn't assume this. I'm for keeping @jralmaraz approach.

> We shouldn't assume this.

Yeah, it’s fine to keep the current switch case as is. But in the current implementation, an error gets returned every time the probe is unknown, so when `runProbeWithRetries` hits the retry limit, it returns an error. Like I mentioned above, this sends it into the previous error handling section and treats everything as a 'Probe errored'. So, if we want to log and write an event as 'Probe unknown', I think the suggested code addition is necessary.
I'd prefer the latter to go into `switch` statement below. As for the former, what about including result into the message, so for any result type the error message would be informative enough?
